brief.name: The made-to-order pendants
brief.objective: Introduce four of HLR’s made-to-order pendants to the email list and send each reader to a pendant’s page.
brief.audience: HLR’s email subscribers. No segment data is on file.
brief.guidance: Vocabulary: made to order, pendant. Tone: the voice contract as written, short lines, one accent word in a headline. No figures; intentions only as tradition or intention.

angle.copy2: The made-to-order fact is the story: the reader’s choice is the first step of the making.
angle.tension: Jewelry usually waits on a shelf; these four wait for the person who will wear them.
angle.scene: the order as the first step of the making
angle.why: It rests on the one fact the pack carries for all four (made to order) and gives the reader a scene: the moment of choosing.

hero.why: States the made-to-order fact in plain words and puts the reader at the start of it; the accent falls on the verb.

hero.copy: A pendant that begins with you
hero.why: Turns the fact into something given to the reader: the piece starts with her choice.

hero.copy: Something to choose slowly this season
hero.why: Places the send in the giving season without promising a delivery date, since none is on file.
A question the reader might ask, answered by the next module: with her choice.

hero.copy: Four pendants, every one made to order
hero.why: Lets the record do the persuading: all four carry made to order in products.json.

subject.why: Says what is inside and the one fact that sets it apart.
Opens a small question the email answers.

subject.copy: Made for the one who chooses it
subject.why: Warm toward the reader, and true of a made-to-order piece.
Ties the send to the season without a date it cannot keep.

subject.copy: Every one of these is made to order
subject.why: The fact as the reason to open.

cta.why: Verb first, two words, and it repeats the angle’s one action.
The plainest route to the four product pages.
A light wink on choosing one of four; warm without flirting.
Frames the click as the start of the making.
The giving season, with no promise of when it arrives.
A statement rather than an order; it reads as an invitation.

vals.body: Each of these four pendants is made to order, so the making begins only once you have picked one. Take your time with the four designs below, and find the one you mean to wear.

vals.headline: The making starts with your choice
vals.body: These four pendants are made to order. None of them is made ahead and set aside: each one begins when you choose it. Look closely, and take the one that feels like yours.

vals.headline: First the choice, then the making
vals.body: Every pendant here is made to order, after it is chosen. So start with the design that holds your eye, and let the making follow.

angle.copy: A pendant worn as a reminder of what you are calling in
angle.tension: An intention set in the morning is gone by noon; something worn stays.
angle.why: Waits on HLR’s C2 ruling; every line would stay intention, never effect.

angle.copy: The giving season: a piece made for one person, chosen for one person
angle.tension: Gifts in November are bought in a rush; a made-to-order piece is chosen on purpose.
angle.why: Needs an order cutoff or delivery window HLR has not given.

angle.copy2: Present each of the designs as a place to start, with the reader’s choice as the beginning.
angle.tension: A lineup of four can read as a catalog; framed as four beginnings, it asks for one decision.
angle.scene: a lineup: four designs, one choice
angle.why: It suits the grid this type carries and keeps the reader on the pieces rather than the process.

angle.copy2: Tell the made-to-order fact as a two-step sequence the reader can follow: you choose, it is made.
angle.tension: Waiting usually feels like a cost; here the wait is the making.
angle.scene: a sequence: the choice, then the making
angle.why: Clear and quick to read, but it draws attention to a wait, and no making time is on file to say how long.

notes.text: Angle not ratified: R1 and its first scene were developed as the recommendation under Eddie’s overnight delegation (2026-10-23). R2 (benefit) and R3 (occasion) stay live; pick again and only the copy below the angle changes.

Products resolved from products.json: element-pendant, sacred-pendant, genesis-pendant, seeker-pendant. Descriptions are empty until HLR’s Shopify export lands, so the copy states no metal, karat, stone, meaning, size or price; the one fact used is made to order (observed.made_to_order on all four).
The subject and preheader were drafted from the voice contract alone: the exemplar file has no subject or preheader lines.

The pack has no favorites yet, so every gate saw historical exemplars only; no measured preference is on file, so the checklist carries the voice contract’s five checks and the brief items, and a human picks.

Type product_listing read live from type-registry-core.json (ratified). The grid’s card names are data-fed from products.json (E06.name), so they are not drafted as options; the footer carries HLR-REQ-01 verbatim in M09 and is not redrafted here.
Every composed string fit its slot budget, so the cut pass changed nothing: cuts lists each mapped string unchanged so fit_check can confirm the budgets.
Revised after the fresh-context review (round 1): “choose” appeared six times, so the body, the grid heading, the preheader and the closing CTA now vary the verb; the hero line and its CTA keep it.
Each headline names its accent word (field accent); the build sets that word in font/style/headline-accent.
The ledger is a test seed (hlr-ledger-0.2.0): its rows are enforced provisionally and no line here is cleared for production until HLR names its claims signer (C2).
